TROCHLEAR (IV) ≠ TRIGEMINAL (V). Trochlear = motor to the DORSAL OBLIQUE only, the ONLY nerve with a DORSAL origin (mesencephalon), decussates; lesion = EXTORSION. Trigeminal = 3 divisions (ophthalmic, maxillary, mandibular), sensory to face + motor to muscles of mastication (slides 21–26).

ABDUCENT (VI) ≠ ACCESSORY (XI). Abducent = lateral rectus + retractor bulbi, orbital fissure, lesion = MEDIAL strabismus. Accessory = trapezius (sole), sternocephalicus, brachiocephalicus, omotransversarius; enters via foramen magnum, exits jugular foramen / tympanooccipital fissure (slides 28–29, 44).

GLOSSOPHARYNGEAL (IX) ≠ HYPOGLOSSAL (XII). IX = taste + general sensation CAUDAL 1/3 of tongue, pharyngeal muscles, parotid + zygomatic glands; passes MEDIAL to external carotid; jugular foramen / tympanooccipital fissure. XII = MOTOR to tongue + geniohyoideus; passes LATERAL to external carotid; its OWN hypoglossal canal (slides 40, 46).

FACE: FACIAL (VII) = MOTOR to muscles of facial expression (+ caudal belly of digastricus). TRIGEMINAL (V) = SENSATION of the face + motor to muscles of MASTICATION (except caudal belly of digastricus). Digastricus is split: rostral belly = V3, caudal belly = VII (slides 26, 30).

OPTIC CANAL = CN II only. ORBITAL FISSURE = CN III, IV, V1 (ophthalmic), VI. Maxillary (V2) = ROUND foramen → alar canal → rostral alar foramen. Mandibular (V3) = OVAL foramen. Ophthalmic and maxillary do NOT share a foramen (slides 25–26).

INTERNAL ACOUSTIC MEATUS = VII + VIII. VII then runs the facial canal and exits the STYLOMASTOID foramen (caudodorsal to tympanic bulla); VIII ends in the membranous labyrinth and does NOT emerge from the skull (slides 30, 35, 64).
JUGULAR FORAMEN (internal opening) / TYMPANOOCCIPITAL FISSURE (external opening) = IX, X, XI. XII has its own HYPOGLOSSAL CANAL, just caudomedial to the tympanooccipital fissure (slides 39, 46).

Strabismus direction = the side of the WORKING muscle: III lesion → LATERAL strabismus (lateral rectus unopposed); VI lesion → MEDIAL strabismus (medial rectus unopposed); IV lesion → EXTORSION (ventral oblique unopposed) (slides 19, 22, 29). Those eye figures are HUMAN (superior/inferior) — in the dog say DORSAL/VENTRAL rectus and oblique.

PUPIL size flip: CN III (parasympathetic) loss → MYDRIASIS (dilated) + ptosis + lateral strabismus. HORNER'S (sympathetic) loss → MIOSIS (constricted) + ptosis + enophthalmos + third-eyelid protrusion. Both have ptosis (slides 19, 56).

⚠️ FLAG — Horner's numbering: slide 56 says lesions can involve '7 and 8 (mesencephalon, upper motor neurons for CNS), 10 (thoracolumbar spinal cord), or 11 (spinal nerves of thoracolumbar region, or sympathetic trunk)'. The same figure's key on slide 53 lists 7 = rostral colliculus and pretectal nuclei, 8 = oculomotor nucleus, 10 = lateral visceral efferent column (thoracic spinal cord), 11 = CRANIAL CERVICAL GANGLION. Use slide 53's labels for the numbers; ask which interpretation of 7/8/11 she wants for Horner's.

⚠️ FLAG — sympathetic source of the pupil: slide 54 (primate caption) says preganglionic neurons are at C8–T1 and synapse in the 'superior cervical ganglion'; slide 56 says 'thoracolumbar'. Superior cervical ganglion (human) = cranial cervical ganglion (dog), which slides 52–53 use. Use 'cranial cervical ganglion'; confirm the segment level in lecture.

⚠️ FLAG — hypoglossal (XII) scope: slide 60 says XII is motor to all tongue skeletal muscles 'with the exception of the palatoglossus'; slide 46 says intrinsic + extrinsic tongue muscles + geniohyoideus; L28 said XII is the ONLY motor nerve to the tongue. The palatoglossus exception is new in L35 — confirm with Dr. Klimek which phrasing to use. Same slide 60 marks vagus (X) tongue taste/general sensory with '?; some discrepancy in the literature' (slide 43 gives vagal taste from the PHARYNX only).

⚠️ FLAG — auriculotemporal: slide 26 note says the auriculotemporal nerve joins the 'dorsal buccal branch of TRIGEMINAL'; the dorsal buccal branch is normally a FACIAL nerve branch (outside knowledge — confirm), and slide 34 says V and VII superficial branches run together. ⚠️ FLAG — gland names: slide 30 says facial parasympathetics go to 'mandibular & sublingual' salivary glands; slide 58 says 'submandibular and sublingual' (figure: 'submaxillary'). Same gland, human vs veterinary name. Use MANDIBULAR salivary gland for the dog.

⚠️ FLAG — origins: slide 23 says V, VI, VII, VIII all originate from the METENCEPHALON but notes its own figure makes VI, VII, VIII look like they come from the myelencephalon (VIII sits on the junction). Slide 9's figure is also miscolored ('This should be blue…' = metencephalon). Go with the slide TEXT.

items.q: Olfactory nerve (I): pathway from nose to brain (slide 13)?

items.q: Olfactory nerve (I) function and fiber type (slides 11, 13)?

items.q: Fun fact, slide 13: how does Naegleria fowleri reach the brain?
items.a: Adheres to the olfactory nerve in the nasal cavity → migrates along it to the olfactory bulb → crosses the cribriform plate into the brain (attracted to chemicals released by the fibers)

items.q: Optic nerve (II) function and fiber type (slides 11, 15)?

items.q: Why is the optic nerve 'technically a tract, not a nerve' (slide 15)?

items.q: What's around the optic nerve in the orbit (slide 15)?
items.a: Periorbita, an extension of the meninges, and the retractor bulbi muscles

items.q: Why does papilledema (optic disc swelling) indicate increased intracranial pressure (slide 15)?
items.a: The optic nerve's meningeal sheath is continuous with the brain's meninges

items.q: In the orbit, which two nerves are very closely associated (slide 20)?
items.a: Optic nerve (II) and oculomotor nerve (III)

items.q: Why lateral strabismus with a CN III lesion (slide 19)?

items.q: Why ptosis with a CN III lesion (slide 19)?

items.q: Why mydriasis with a CN III lesion (slide 19)?

items.q: Ventrolateral skull view: openings, rostral → caudal (slides 63–64)?
items.a: Ethmoidal foramina, optic canal, orbital fissure, rostral alar foramen, caudal alar foramen, oval foramen, stylomastoid foramen, tympanic bulla, tympanooccipital fissure, hypoglossal canal
